_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); machinery and engines signals

pit_profile.why: 'Caterpillar is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives' (FY2010 10-K, Item 1); 'Caterpillar products and product support services are sold worldwide into a variety of highly competitive markets'; 'The demand for our products and services tends to be cyclical and can be significantly reduced in an economic environment characterized by higher unemployment, lower consumer spending, lower corporate earnings and lower levels of government and business investment.' and 'The energy and mining industries are major users of our machines and engines.' (Item 1A): the 10-K calls the demand for its own products cyclical (BKR's 'Our business is cyclical'), so CYCLICAL from the FY2010 10-K; no disruption theme is live for it

classification.quality_note: 'Caterpillar is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives' (FY2010 10-K, Item 1); 'Caterpillar products and product support services are sold worldwide into a variety of highly competitive markets'; 'The demand for our products and services tends to be cyclical and can be significantly reduced in an economic environment characterized by higher unemployment, lower consumer spending, lower corporate earnings and lower levels of government and business investment.' and 'The energy and mining industries are major users of our machines and engines.' (Item 1A): the 10-K calls the demand for its own products cyclical (BKR's 'Our business is cyclical'), so CYCLICAL from the FY2010 10-K; no disruption theme is live for it. cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 1.12x; +34% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +1.89; conservative 2yr +36%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -61.5%/yr (worst year FY01-FY10, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +25.2%/yr (FY11 guide + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +25.2%/yr (FY01-FY10 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +60.9%/yr (best 2-yr run FY01-FY10); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: CAT (retrospective, 2011-05-20) ◐ WATCHLIST — Ratio B 1.12x (89.5% downside to Bear $11 / +80.2% upside to Bull $188) | Adj composite 3.88 vs market 1.99: gap +1.89 [UNDERVALUED] | +34% above the EPP floor $78 (12x FY11E $6.50) | Conservative 2-yr case: +35.8% total (+17.9%/yr) | At 16.1x FY11E the 15% hurdle price $138 sits at or below the BASE case; Machinery sales +75.9% in Q1 2011, forward revenues +22.1-26.8% (FY11 sales and revenues guide); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
